metrics.safe_success: fraction of episodes that reach the goal without any collision (per run, then mean over runs)
metrics.intervention: sum of interventions / sum of replanning cycles over the successful episodes of a run (mean over runs)
metrics.horizon_s: mean number of control steps of the successful episodes x 0.01 s (mean over runs)

fig4.source: values digitised from the Fig. 4 rasters of the arXiv PDF (v1 and v2 embed identical images); 'read_manually' marks partly occluded markers
notes: '5 random seeds' in the paper are 5 DP checkpoints (epochs 1250/1500/1750/2000 of one training run + the epoch-1900 checkpoint of an earlier training), each evaluated on env seeds 0-99; Gibbs has 4 checkpoints (no epoch 1900) and incomplete runs (32-100 episodes).

The paper plot was made with an unpublished variant of generate_paper_plot.py (no w=0.10 point, different styling); the stored runs in results/paper reproduce all JM2D and DP horizon points and all qualitative claims, but not the RAIL horizon (stored runs 0.55-1.17 s longer), RAIL safe-success at w=0.25 (0.852 vs 0.908) and the Gibbs horizon at w<=0.05 (2.4-2.6 s vs 3.06 s).

Fig. 4 DP/RAIL re-run: the stored DP and RAIL runs used code that fed the DP the current frame twice (fixed before the Table 1 runs of 2025-04-28). The shipped Fig. 4 uses DP/RAIL re-runs with the released code (results/fig4_rerun, 5 checkpoints x 100 seeds) and the stored JM2D/Gibbs runs. The DP re-run matches the paper well; the RAIL re-run does not reproduce the printed RAIL horizon (still 0.37-0.99 s longer) or safe success, so the source of the printed RAIL curve remains unknown (likely a run set or configuration not stored here).
